title: Nearly 1,000 Arrested in France as Cost-of-Living Protests Face Violent Extremists
snippet: French police detained nearly 1,000 people on Saturday after cost-of-living demonstrations were hijacked by radical agitators, resulting in severe injuries and heavy clashes.
content:
PARIS — French authorities arrested nearly 1,000 people on Saturday as nationwide cost-of-living demonstrations devolved into clashes, with police confronting what officials described as an "extremely elevated level of violence" from radical groups.

While broad marches over rising expenses initially passed without incident across several French cities, black-clad extremists and far-left factions disrupted the demonstrations, throwing projectiles and launching fireworks at riot police to provoke confrontations.

Escalating Clashes and Injuries

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reported that at least two people suffered severe injuries during the violence. In the southern city of Toulouse, a 20-year-old man reportedly had his fingers blown off, while another severe injury was recorded in Clermont-Ferrand. Details surrounding the exact circumstances of the injuries remain under investigation.

The Saturday arrest total represented a sharp increase in early detentions compared to the previous week, when an initial wave of demonstrations spiraled into widespread looting that resulted in 2,700 total arrests. However, Nunez noted that enhanced law enforcement tactics—including proactive stop-and-search operations and heavier deployment around commercial centers—significantly reduced the scale of property damage and looting this time around.

Extremist Factions Surface

In the capital city of Paris, the main peaceful march was overtaken during its final stages. According to Nunez, several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the procession, including an estimated 500 rioters who engaged officers in intense street battles for nearly two hours before being dispersed.

The weekend demonstrations also marked a new political flashpoint. In southern coastal cities such as Cannes and Montpellier, authorities for the first time reported the appearance of far-right agitators who actively sought out violent clashes with ultra-left groups or claimed to act as vigilantes protecting local storefronts.

French security forces remain on high alert throughout the weekend, maintaining a heavy presence in major metropolitan areas to prevent further overnight chaos.
